message.content: In domestic cats (and by extension in lions), the presence of a mane in male lions is often cited as a **dominant** trait. The gene that controls the development of the mane is inherited in a dominant fashion—if a male lion carries at least one copy of the “mane” allele, he will develop a mane, whereas females (who typically lack a mane) do not carry the allele in the same way. This dominant trait is one of the most noticeable genetic differences between male and female lions.
